summary: K2 (8,611 m), on Pakistan's border in Gilgit-Baltistan's Karakoram range, is about 240 m shorter than Everest (8,849 m) but far more dangerous, which is why climbers call it the Savage Mountain. Per summit, K2's death rate has historically been many times Everest's: close to 1 death for every 4 summits until about 2000, and still roughly 13-14% by 2022, against roughly 1-4% on Everest. It is steeper and more technical, its weather is harsher and less predictable, and most deaths happen during or just after the summit push (including the Bottleneck). It was the last of the world's fourteen 8,000 m peaks to be climbed in winter: ten Nepali climbers reached the top on 16 January 2021. Pakistan's Muhammad Ali Sadpara, from Skardu, the only Pakistani to have climbed eight of the 14 eight-thousanders and the first to climb Nanga Parbat in winter, lost his life on K2 in February 2021.
audience: Pakistani families and young people who love the northern areas and enjoy surprising facts about their own country

facts.fact: K2 is 8,611 metres high, the second-highest mountain on Earth.
facts.source: Guinness World Records: First winter ascent of K2

facts.fact: Mount Everest is about 8,849 metres high, so K2 is roughly 240 metres shorter.
K2 is in the Karakoram range on the Pakistan-China border, in Gilgit-Baltistan.
Until about 2000, K2's death rate was close to one death for every four summits (about 25-29%).
facts.source: Yahoo/Outside: Is K2 becoming less savage?; himalayantrekking.com

facts.fact: By 2022, after many more successful climbs, K2's death rate per summit was still roughly 13-14%.
facts.source: Statista; Wikipedia: List of deaths on eight-thousanders

facts.fact: Everest's death rate per summit is much lower, roughly 1-4% depending on how it is counted.
Most deaths on K2 above 8,000 m happen during or just after the summit push.
K2 is steeper and more technical than Everest, with harsher and less predictable weather.
K2 was the last of the world's fourteen 8,000-metre peaks to be climbed in winter.
A team of 10 Nepali climbers made the first winter ascent of K2 on 16 January 2021.
facts.source: Guinness World Records; Al Jazeera; Dawn

facts.fact: Muhammad Ali Sadpara from Skardu was the only Pakistani to have climbed eight of the 14 eight-thousanders and made the first winter ascent of Nanga Parbat; he died on K2 in February 2021 during a winter attempt.
facts.source: Dawn: A heart as big as K2; Al Jazeera (Feb 2021)

facts.fact: K2 was first climbed in 1954 by an Italian expedition.

avoid: Exact single death-rate number as fact (counts differ); use 'about 1 in 4 historically' and 'still much higher than Everest'
Sensationalising deaths; mention Ali Sadpara with respect
Saying K2 is the most dangerous mountain overall (Annapurna's rate is sometimes higher)
Using climber footage as if it were a specific named expedition
